findings.claim: The client-secret verifier can still pass an actual Supabase service-role JWT if it is assigned to a public/non-service-role variable name.
findings.evidence: The acceptance criterion requires “Client examples never expose service-role credentials,” but `scanClientExamples` only rejects names/patterns such as `FLINT_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `SERVICE_ROLE...=`, `service[_-]?role[_-]?key`, `flint_sk_...`, and `VITE_...SECRET|PRIVATE|SERVICE`; it never decodes JWT payloads or detects a service-role credential value such as `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=<JWT whose payload has "role":"service_role">`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add value-level detection for JWT credentials by parsing base64url JWT payloads found in scanned text and rejecting payloads with `role: "service_role"` or equivalent server-only claims; add a regression where a service-role JWT is assigned to a misleading public variable name.
